messages:
Kira Thompson: Hey folks — Support/CS Q as we prep for Shadow Evals beta enablement. Getting enterprise questions already:
1) “Do you store prompts/outputs from shadow runs?”
2) “What’s retention + where is it stored?”
3) “Can we opt out entirely / disable shadowing per route?”

Need a customer-facing blurb we can paste into tickets + a 1-pager for CSMs. @Marissa Cole @Naomi Feldman @Kevin Osei

Marissa Cole: +1. Also some customers are confused by “shadow traffic” terminology. They assume it’s request replay / could impact their live responses.

Marissa Cole: Proposed high-level phrasing (draft):
- Shadow Evals runs a sampled copy of *eligible* requests asynchronously against a candidate model/config.
- Primary response path is unchanged; shadow execution never blocks or alters user responses.
- If shadow capacity is constrained, we drop shadow runs (best-effort) rather than impacting production.

But I need the retention / opt-out specifics locked.

Naomi Feldman: For customer-facing, we should be crisp and conservative.
What we can say (aligned w/ security review):
- By default: we retain *derived evaluation metrics* (latency/cost deltas, judge/rubric scores, safety outcomes) and minimal request metadata needed to aggregate (route, region, model ids, timestamps).
- Prompt + completion payload storage is *configurable* and can be disabled.
- If payload retention is enabled: we store redacted payloads (per configured redaction rules) for a limited time window for debugging/audit of scoring. Access is restricted (least privilege) + audited.
- Data residency: stored in the same region boundary as the request processing / customer’s configured residency controls.

We should avoid stating exact days in Slack unless we’re certain (we can reference the doc + “customer configurable”).

Kevin Osei: Agree w/ Naomi. For a support macro, I’d include explicit opt-out knobs:
- Customer can disable Shadow Evals globally (account-level kill switch)
- Customer can disable per route
- Customer can set sampling to 0%
- Customer can set retention to “metrics-only” (no prompts/outputs) or “no retention” if that’s their requirement

Also call out that any payload access requires elevated role and is audited. That tends to unblock SOC2 questionnaires.

Kira Thompson: This helps. What do we say when they ask “Do you train on our data?” (we always get that one)

Naomi Feldman: Standard: we do not use customer prompts/outputs to train foundation models. Shadow Evals data follows the same policy as inference logs: only used to provide/secure the service, per contract + DPA, and per customer logging/retention settings.

Paula Mendes: From the rollouts side: we should make clear that shadowing is an *evaluation signal*, not automatic routing change.
- Shadow Evals can inform rollout guardrails (e.g., halt canary if judge win-rate drops)
- But it does not change the serving model unless the customer configures an explicit rollout policy

This reduces fear of “silent model change.”

Elliot Price: I can turn this into a short “Customer FAQ” section for docs + support macro. Before I do: can we provide a stable internal link for exact retention defaults and how to request changes?

Kevin Osei: Use go link from the policy doc once it’s finalized. For now, we can reference “Shadow Evals Data Retention & Redaction” in Confluence (Security & Compliance space).

Marissa Cole: For the macro, I’d suggest something like:

“Shadow Evals mirrors a sampled subset of your production requests to a candidate model/config *asynchronously*. Your end users still receive the primary response; shadow execution is best-effort and will drop rather than affect your latency/SLOs.

Data handling: By default, Shadow Evals retains derived evaluation metrics and minimal metadata for aggregation. Storage of prompts/outputs is configurable and can be disabled. If enabled, payloads are redacted per configured rules, access is restricted and audited, and retention is limited/customer-controlled. Data is stored in-region consistent with your residency settings.

Controls: You can opt out at any time via global disable, per-route disable, or setting sampling to 0%. We can also configure metrics-only mode (no payload retention).”

Naomi Feldman: +1, with one tweak: avoid “mirrors your production requests” without clarifier — some folks interpret as replay with side effects.
Maybe: “copies the request payload and runs it against a shadow target” + “does not execute tools/actions.”

Marissa Cole: Good catch. We should mention tool calling explicitly. For Chat/Responses w/ tool calls: shadow path won’t execute external side effects (or we stub/disable tools). Can we state that confidently?

Kevin Osei: Yes, for beta scope: shadow targets run in “no-side-effects” mode. Tools disabled by default; if customer wants to judge tool-call JSON, we evaluate the *proposed* tool call but do not execute.

Kira Thompson: Perfect — that’s a frequent concern.

Elliot Price: Action items:
- I’ll draft a Support macro + 1-pager FAQ for CSMs with the approved language.
- @Naomi Feldman / @Kevin Osei can you add a “safe wording” section to the retention/redaction doc we can quote verbatim?

Naomi Feldman: Yes. I’ll add a customer-safe paragraph + what we should *not* promise (e.g., exact retention days unless contractually set).

Marissa Cole: I’ll also update the Console UI copy: “Shadow Evals (best-effort, non-impacting)” + a tooltip that says “Shadow runs never affect end-user responses; they may be dropped under load.”

Kira Thompson: Thanks all. Once Elliot has a draft, I’ll test it on the open enterprise ticket and see what follow-ups we get.
